header.running_head: Honouring People Despite Differences in Opinion and Deed

blocks.text: their father's (by not taking any of their possessions for ourselves)."[^1]

Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was once asked whether the people who fought him in the Battle of Jamal were Mushrikeen. He replied, "It is from Shirk that we fled." "Were they then Munaafiqeen?" he was asked further. Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "Munaafiqeen very seldom think of Allaah (whereas these did so very often)." "Then what were they?" came the final question. Hadhrat Ali (RA) explained, "They were simply our brothers who rebelled against us."[^2]
Hadhrat Ali (RA) Welcomes the Son of Hadhrat Talha (RA) and his Statements Concerning Hadhrat Talha (RA) and Hadhrat Zubayr (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Habeebah the freed slave of Hadhrat Talha (RA) says that it was after the Battle of Jamal that he once went to Hadhrat Ali (RA) in the company of Hadhrat Imraan the son of Hadhrat Talha (RA)[^3]. Hadhrat Ali (RA) welcomed him most warmly and called him close. He then said, "I wish that Allaah would make your father and I amongst those about whom He says:

blocks.arabic_text: وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِيْ صُدُوْرِهِمْ مِّنْ غِلٍّ إِخْوَانًا عَلٰى سُرُرٍ مُّتَقٰبِلِيْنَ
blocks.text: We shall remove any ill-feelings that may be in their breasts. As brothers they will be seated on couches, facing each other."

Addressing Hadhrat Imraan in the most endearing terms, Hadhrat Ali (RA) then asked him about all the wives and children of Hadhrat Talha (RA) by name. He further said, "We have taken possession of your lands these past few years only for fear that others may usurp them." Addressing one of his men, Hadhrat Ali (RA) instructed, "Take him to Ibn Qardha and tell him to hand over to this man the revenue due to him for all these years together with his land."
There were two men sitting in the corner, one of whom was Haarith A'war. They remarked, "Allaah is more just than that! How is it that they had been fighting us and still be our brothers in Jannah?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Get up you two and get away to the furthest of Allaah's lands. Who else can the verse be referring to if it does not refer to Talha and I? (Hadhrat Ali (RA) then addressed Hadhrat Talha (RA)'s son saying,) My dear brother's son! Come to me whenever you need something."[^4]

A narration of Hadhrat Rib'ee bin Hiraash adds that (when the two men passed their comment), Hadhrat Ali (RA) screamed so loud that the scream could have brought a palace tumbling down. He said, "Who will such people be if they are not Talha and I?"
Hadhrat Talha (RA) and Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) both fought against Hadhrat Ali (RA) in the Battle of Jamal.
Bayhaqi (Vol.8 Pg.173) and Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.224).
